BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Preliminary points

- **Every clause was reviewed, including those marked [STANDARD].** The Seller's "Reviewer Efficiency Note" says [STANDARD] clauses are cleared, and the preamble says positions are "FINAL", "settled at principal level" and "market standard". Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3, these labels are counterparty assertions. They are not confirmed instructions through our authority process. No Amelia Frost written authority has been given for any fallback.
- **The facts may be out of date.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026, so the DD facts need refreshing before we rely on them. Facts verified by documents should be kept separate from the Seller's assertions.

## Issue-by-issue review

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at 25%. The 20% figure matches our conditional fallback, but that fallback needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. None has been given, and a matching number does not clear the change.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with recovery from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the deductible structure removes first-dollar recovery. "~1% market" is an unverified assertion.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months. Any limitation is to apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. Separate periods for other categories.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost approval, which has not been given. The "applies to all Claims" default would also silently shorten the Title, Tax, IP and indemnity periods.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Title and capacity subject to the general caps and time limits, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and exclusion from the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title and capacity go to the core of what we are buying. A 20% cap on a title failure is not a simplification; it is a reallocation of fundamental risk.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert an express carve-out. This is non-waivable under our playbook, and no one on our side may concede it.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Delete DL 1.1–1.2 and accept only the specific disclosures (DL 2–10) to the extent they are fair. Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure is expressly rejected in our playbook. The DL 1.4 non-admission wording also needs review so that it does not undercut those specific disclosures.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or that was discoverable from the data room or public records (clause 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must use named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry.
- **Recommendation:** Delete. Constructive "discoverable" knowledge, combined with SPA-N-006, would exclude almost every claim. A knowledge qualifier must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent, plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and make it a hard Condition Precedent. Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m, DD-002), and DL 2 confirms that no consent or condition evidence has been provided. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** A security release to be provided after Completion. About AUD 3.2m is outstanding.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Require a payout letter and deed of release as Completion deliverables. DL 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and undischarged. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval, neither of which we have.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** DD-005 bonuses plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Debt deduction, or demonstrably funded by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Add a line item and confirm the on-costs. The Company will be the employer at payment, so an unitemised liability falls on us. DL 5 is silent on payroll tax and superannuation, so the on-cost amount needs to be confirmed rather than assumed.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering title and ownership defects in the Ironquay materials, while preserving the SOW3 payment cure.
- **Recommendation:** Broaden it. Also seek evidence of cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment. Under DD-004 clause 7.3, transfer depends on payment of every SOW3 fee, and DL 4 confirms that no receipt or assignment is in the data room. The AUD 180,000 open amount (DD-010) is unverified either way, so it should not be treated as either owing or paid.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, investigation, and regular updates before Completion, with a covenant and appropriate warranty or indemnity protection.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the materiality characterisation and add pre-Completion covenants. The scope of about 1,240 records, whether anyone accessed the file, and any notification obligation are all unresolved (DL 6). We should assume neither a confirmed breach nor its absence, and we should not put forward any numeric demand.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** AUD 330,000 (3 × AUD 110,000) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment first, covering whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course (DD-008 and DD-011 read together).
- **Recommendation:** Hold the position pending diligence. Neither accept the "ordinary course" label nor automatically classify the renewals as Debt or a price deduction. DL 8 itself says these points are unstated.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** A single general regime applies to all Claims, and Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate Title, Tax, IP, payment-indemnity and covenant regimes, with no general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Draft express carve-outs from clauses 12 and 13 for each category. The clause 12.3/13 default and the clause 9.3/12.8/20.5 "all Claims" wording together create a hidden override.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, such as an ASIC search, PPSR search, constitution and board resolutions, share certificates, and confirmation that no options or rights exist.
- **Recommendation:** Reject reliance on DD-012 alone. It is a supplied internal record, and DL 10 concedes we have not independently verified it.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Settled under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** These terms treated as OPEN.
- **Recommendation:** Keep them open and reserve our position. Nothing in our record shows agreement. We should not assume unlimited liability or that the issue has been resolved, and should negotiate bespoke caps and periods.

## Next steps

1. Mark up the SPA to the playbook positions above, and strike the [STANDARD]/FINAL characterisations in our covering response.
2. Do not deploy any fallback, whether the 20% cap, the 18-month period or a post-Completion Riverlark release, without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft.
3. Request refreshed facts as at a current date covering:
   - Bluefen consent status
   - the Riverlark payout figure
   - DD-006 investigation status
   - Ironquay payment evidence
   - bonus on-costs
   - Sandbar terms
